utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom and those assisting us just outside the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-95-10/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ranko Cesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning, Mr. Cesic. Good morning, Defence counsel. Good morning, counsel for the Prosecution. We are here to have a status conference. I have a few items on the agenda. The first is disclosure, where we stand, whether there are any problems. The second is whether there are any -- whether there's any progress made between the parties up to this moment in compromising on the establishment of facts. The third would be the -- whether there's any problem in respect of the health situation of Mr. Cesic. And is there anything you'd like to add to the agenda? Of course, I'm aware that a few other things are pending. We have a proposed amendment to the indictment. It's not necessary to discuss it here, but if one of the parties would like to say anything about it, and then not the substance of the matter but perhaps procedural issues or questions, then of course I would give an opportunity for that. So if there's anything the parties would like to add to the agenda, I'll give them an opportunity. But before doing so, perhaps just for the completeness of the transcript, in asking the Defence whether they would like to add anything that they give the appearances as well so that we are complete for the transcript. Could I first ask the Defence to give the appearances, and to ask whether there's anything you'd like to add to the agenda. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Vojislav Nedic. I'm an attorney at law from Belgrade, and I appear for the accused Cesic. Next to me is Ms. Trlaic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would the Defence like to add something to the agenda?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at the present, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Judge Orie. My name is Mark Harmon representing the Office of the Prosecutor this morning. Appearing with me to my right, Mr. Vladimir Tochilovsky, to his right, Mr. Thomas Hannis, and the case manager, Ms. Susan Grogan, case manager. We do not wish to add anything to the agenda this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, very much Mr. Harmon. I also was informed that one of the parties would like to address the Court or perhaps the accused would like to address me in closed session. Is that information right? I'm just looking to Prosecution, Defence, and you, Mr. Cesic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not hear the interpretation, so I didn't understand you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll repeat what I said to both counsel for the Prosecution, counsel for the Defence, and you, that I was informed that someone would like to address me in closed session. If that is true, we'll have to find a moment when to discuss the matter of which I, of course, do not know yet what it is about. Is there in request for closed session during this Status Conference on an issue not yet mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At present, I do have a problem. Since I have no counsel, I submitted an application, but this has not resolved. The attorneys present are only provisional, and this is a problem for me because I have to start preparing my defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's an issue you would like to add to the agenda. We'll see whether and in what detail we can discuss this matter because as far as I'm informed, a request has been made to the Registry. A decision has been given, or at least a letter has been sent to you by the Registry which seems to contain a decision. And that's where it stands at this very moment, as far as I can see. But if there would be any practical matter related to it, we could discuss this. Please be seated, Mr. Cesic. Let's first start, then, with the agenda as I proposed it to be, and start with the disclosure. I'm not aware of any specific problem at this very moment in respect of disclosure. And since we are -- the stage of the proceedings we are in, one would expect if there would be a problem, that it would come from the Defence. I would first give the Defence an opportunity to make any comment on the disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence, Your Honour, has received the decision of the 22nd of November, and we have no objections to such a decision. As far as we are concerned, everything is in order. There is an order to the Prosecution that they should submit the third amended indictment, and we are expecting this. Apart from what the accused has raised, that is, that he wishes to change his Defence counsel, we have nothing to add. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is not specific on disclosure that you tell me; it's more about the indictment and the consequences of earlier decisions. Does the Defence have confidence that they have received all the material they are entitled to receive under the disclosure rules?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our view, as regards the case against Jelisic who has already been convicted, we have not received all the documents needed for the Defence. But we wish to say that we still have problems in preparing the Defence because the accused is refusing to have any contacts with us. So with your leave, Your Honour, I wish to say that we, as Defence counsel of the accused Cesic, also wish to withdraw. And I have submitted this to the Registry in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- you're trying to come to the issue I would like to discuss later. My question at this very moment is whether you have received all the information, documents, that the Prosecution is obliged to provide to you under Rule 66 and following. You say that in respect of the Jelisic case, who has already been convicted, that you have not received all the documents needed for the Defence, what specific documents have you not received and when did you specifically ask for these documents to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In September, as far as I can recall, we asked for the documents from the Jelisic case. We do not have the transcript. At present, I can't say precisely, but we consider that we needed all the documents related to that case because it seems to be connected with this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harmon, would the Prosecution please -- so I now understand that the issue is that the Defence has asked for all documents including all transcripts of the Jelisic case and that they have not received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Orie, two things: One, I do not and have never received a request for documents from the Jelisic case. The Jelisic documents are public documents. They are public transcripts. They are available to the Defence and have been available. That case was concluded many years ago. In respect of pre-trial discovery and disclosure, we have completed our disclosure to the Defence. We have completed all our Rule 66 disclosure to the Defence. In fact, we have gone beyond what we are legally obligated to disclose, and we believe that we have now completed all pre-trial disclosure obligations, Rule 66 and Rule 68 that apply in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nedic, is there any -- did you send a letter to the Prosecution explaining on the basis of which Rule you wanted documents to be disclosed, apart from public documents, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At present, I'm unable to say because I have several assistants in my team, so I cannot say at present. But I do allow that Mr. Harmon may be right, and this is a problem that can easily be overcome. The Defence will do everything it can to overcome this problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is a problem, since you are telling me that it's easy to overcome this problem, I expect this to be settled before we have a 65 ter meeting, perhaps in the near future. So please, check what you asked for, what was the basis in the Rules on which you asked these documents. Please ask yourself whether you wish to have access to documents that are already publicly available. Then see whether there's any remaining problem, and then of course, as the pre-trial judge, I would very much appreciate if the problem really would be overcome. That means that at this very moment, we have no further disclosure issues to discuss. Second issue, as far as I'm concerned, the progress the parties have made in compromising on the establishment of facts in this case. I do understand from you, Mr. Nedic, that you have some difficulties because of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, you understand correctly. The problem lies in my communication with my client who refuses to communicate with me. And it is, therefore, extremely difficult for me to defend him properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. And do I also understand that this is an obstacle for ongoing communication with the Prosecution to see whether there could be any facts established by the parties, that is, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. consent between the parties on the establishment of facts? Mr. Harmon, therefore I take it it is correct that the Prosecution could not give any further information in this respect as to such facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct, Judge Orie. We're prepared at any time to meet with the representative of Mr. Cesic to discuss those issues. We have not done so to date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it turns out that we have a serious problem here. Mr. Cesic, I am informed that you'd like to change counsel. You have filed a request to that extent, and you have been informed by the Registry that the counsel you'd like to be assigned to you is not fulfilling the requirements, especially not in view of the mastering of one of the official languages of the Tribunal. And apart from that, also his specific experience in criminal cases. This decision has been sent to you in a short letter by the Registrar. The Chamber has not received any appeal on that, and you might be aware that usually decisions of the Registry are not under a full appeal of the Chamber to the extent that the Chamber would have the competence to review such a decision and take over the responsibilities of the Registry. There is a clear distinction between the Registry and the Chamber. And I'm not saying that such decisions cannot be reviewed, but it's not the case that the Chamber takes over in reviewing such case the full responsibilities of the Registry. But if there would be anything, although there's no request for review filed, if there would be anything you'd like to tell me about it, please do so. If you can do it in open session, fine. If you cannot do it in open session, then please ask for closed session. I would like to make one observation. In the beginning, you said you have no Defence counsel. That must be a mistake. You have Defence counsel assigned to you. The present situation is that you would wish to have other Defence counsel assigned to you. This wish has not been fulfilled, at least not until now. I want to make it quite clear to you that whatever happens in this situation, you cannot tell the Court later that you had no Defence counsel. It's your own choice whether you want to communicate with Defence counsel assigned to you. But if this would result in, let's say, a failure to file documents in time or whatever, as long as Mr. Nedic is your Defence counsel, he will assist you. If you do not communicate with him, you are the one who has to take full responsibility for the consequences of that. I want this to be quite clear before I invite you to make whatever submissions you'd like to make in this respect.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I haven't had the interpretation the entire time, so I do not understand anything that is being said here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say during the last 20 minutes or just on what I said? But even this might not be translated, so it's of no use. Is there -- could someone check what we have on channel 6, I take it, here? Yes, I was not aware that Mr. Cesic was all the time on the wrong channel. Mr. Cesic, let me just trying to summarise, unless you say I want the whole discussion to be repeated, because you're fully entitled to follow whatever is said in this Court. But if you would say a summary could help me, but I do understand that you're in a very specific situation where communication with Defence counsel is problematic. Do you want that we restart, or do you or could we start and try to summarise what has been said until now? It's dangerous to start early in the morning. I suggest that we have a break, that we restart the Status Conference, and that the parties try to be as brief as possible, but repeat so that the accused can hear it whatever has been said. But we could do it, I take it, in less time than we used until now because we know more or less what to expect. I don't know whether for technical reasons it could be done even before 9.30 where I do understand that another case starts at 9.30. Would there be a possibility to restart later this day during this morning? There is no possibility to sit again this morning, so my decision is that we restart the entire Status Conference and finish with it if possible within half an hour. The interpreters have no sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague Trlaic also has no audio either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll speak in the microphone not because I've got something to say but just in order to check whether the system functions properly. I have to continue to speak without having anything to say which is for lawyers usually not a major problem, but... No translation. We have B/C/S translation, but no French. Mr. Nedic, we still have technical problems. The interpreters' booth have no power in their microphones as far as I can see. I've got an entirely different question to you. You are at this moment in The Hague. When was -- I see that everything seems to be repaired, but nevertheless I'll finish my question to you. When was your departure from The Hague scheduled?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not receive interpretation. I've understood your question partially, however I did not receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was on the wrong channel. My question was when your departure from The Hague, you and co-counsel, were scheduled?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [In English] We are staying in Hotel Staten, and we will come back tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you want to return tomorrow morning, yes. Now, a final check. What languages do we have available? Do we have an English translation? Not necessary because I speak English. Could you speak a few words, Mr. Nedic, in your own language so that we know that your words are translated into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least interpretation into English words.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear now well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... because everyone was automatically reset on channel 0. Now you can hear me. So the translation, English/B/C/S is functioning. I just heard that B/C/S/English is functioning as well. [Interpretation] I would like to say a few words in French now so that we can establish for sure whether the interpretation from French is going unhindered. [In English] It looks as if now all problems have been overcome. I was just informed that the whole building is on a generator at this moment, and if we would return to the normal power supply, that we have to go through the whole exercise again. So I would have to again speak French. Is there any idea on how long we are on a generator? If that would be more than half an hour, we could finish. Okay. This courtroom is needed for another case in approximately half an hour. Mr. Nedic, you're expected to return tomorrow. If we give it a chance, the worst thing that could happen is that we have to do it again. The best thing is that we can finish. If we leave this courtroom, we have to find another moment anyhow to restart. So we'll give it a time. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-95-10/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ranko Cesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, may I have the appearances briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, on behalf of the Prosecutor's Office, name is Mark Harmon, appearing with my is Mr. Vladimir Tochilovsky, Mr. Thomas Hannis, and to my far right Ms. Susan Grogan, the case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. May I have the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Vojislav Nedic. I'm an attorney from Belgrade. I'm Defence counsel for the accused Cesic and to my left is my colleague Vesna Trliac, a member of my Defence team.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are still not sure that the accused has the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, has now the accused -- can you hear me, Mr. Cesic, in a language you understand? That's the question I should have put to you in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. On the agenda are disclosure issues and progress in communication between the parties in order to establish facts they can agree upon. And third, the health situation of Mr. Cesic. I was informed that the request by Mr. Cesic to be that new Defence counsel would be assigned is also one of the issues that should be discussed. I was informed that the request by Mr. Cesic to be that new Defence counsel would be assigned is also one of the issues that should be discussed. Mr. Cesic, I leave it up to you whether it should be discussed in open or in closed session. As far as disclosure is concerned, Mr. Nedic, could you give -- are there any complaints about the way the Prosecution has fulfilled until now its disclosure obligations under the Rules, that is, Rule 66 and 68? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there would be any remaining problems, I'd like you to communicate this with the Prosecution and see where it stands so that it could be further discussed and on a 65 ter meeting to be scheduled for the beginning of next year. Mr. Harmon, is there any disclosure issue that should be discussed at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Orie, there are none. We believe that we have completed all of our disclosure under Rule 66 and Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so I invite the parties to communicate whatever problems that would either come up or might be remaining. Then Mr. Nedic, the progress in communication between Defence and Prosecution, as far as the agreement on established facts is concerned, you inform me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Simply speaking, due to the difficulties that I have in communicating with my client, or rather the absence of any communication whatsoever, my communication with the Prosecutor is difficult as well. However, I am prepared to speak to Mr. Harmon at any time, especially since that is in the interest of my client. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, is there any observation to be made from the Prosecution side, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We, of course, are always available to discuss the matters that relate to the progress of this case and the disposition of this case and discovery in this case with Mr. Nedic and anyone else who may appear on behalf of Mr. Cesic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Cesic, this brings me to an issue that seems to be of importance at this very moment. The issue is that you asked for another Defence counsel to be assigned, that the Registry has sent you a letter in which it is explained to you that the counsel you would like to be assigned is not meeting the requirements for assignment, is not on the list, and there seem to be -- is not on a list, so therefore he cannot be assigned at this very moment. Could you tell us what your position is because I do understand from what Mr. Nedic told us that you do not communicate with present counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't go to see them only yesterday, and I submitted my request two months ago. Mr. Nedic's work or rather lack of it has been going on for quite a while. Basically, he hasn't done his work from the very beginning. This is why I wanted another attorney to be appointed to me. I have received no materials whatsoever from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please. Mr. Cesic, would it be a good idea to go into private session when we discuss behaviour of counsel which might have consequences, especially because this meeting as such is not scheduled to hear complaints about counsel. Therefore, I think, unless counsel would say, "I have no problem whatsoever to discuss the matter in open Court," then of course, there would be no reason for that. But if you, Mr. Nedic, would prefer, because your activities as counsel might have a -- it's not only that criticism on that could come up, and I wonder whether that should be done in private session. But if you want to respond, then of course your activities as Defence counsel might become public as well where you could also consider this not to be something for the general public. I also have to remind you that if you discuss your activities as Defence counsel in the presence of Prosecution, then of course also the confidentiality of your relationship with your client might be at stake. So whenever you feel that it should not be done, not even in the presence of the Prosecution, please indicate so. Would you please express yourself whether you would like to discuss the matter in private session and whether you have any objection against the Prosecution still be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like it to be in a closed session. I would like this problem to be discussed in a closed session since it covers sensitive issues in the relationship between attorney and client. As far as the presence of the Prosecutor is concerned, I do not object to them being present. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Private session I take it would do, otherwise we have to pull down all the curtains. And private session would be agreeable to you, Mr. Nedic? No one hears what you say. Yes? Okay, then we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are now again in open session. I have to briefly repeat what I said over the last two minutes, that is, that the character of the case might justify the expectation that hearing the case at trial might not take as long as many other cases take in this Tribunal, and that a second issue that might come up is a possible referral of the case under Rule 11 bis, and whenever the parties have ever thought about the possibility of the application of 11 bis. And if so, please inform me on what their thoughts would be on that issue. And if not, perhaps find Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. an opportunity for themselves to consider this aspect of the case. May I first ask you, Mr. Nedic, whether you ever considered this case to qualify for referral under Rule 11 bis? That is, a referral back to the authorities of state in whose territory the crime was committed or in which the accused was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not considered that issue. I believe that in that case, one would need to have the consent of the client, Mr. Cesic. And I was unable to establish communication with him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can imagine that in order to express yourself on the issue, you would need the consent of the client, whether for a referral you would need the consent of the client, that's a different matter. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the case itself would take less than one month to prosecute on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. There's limited evidence in this case. It's a very specific case. It's eyewitness testimony about events. This is not a complex case to try before this Tribunal. On the issue of whether this case qualifies under 11 bis, certainly we've never had a conversation, counsel and I. And that is something that's worth exploring. On the other hand, there's a condition precedent to such a referral. We would need to be satisfied that the courts function properly in the Former Yugoslavia before this case should be referred back. While this may be a small case, there were many victims in this case. And the crimes themselves were serious crimes, and we would need to be satisfied that those crimes could be properly addressed by functioning courts that would do a proper job in assessing the evidence in this case. There are other considerations as well, but I needn't burden the Chamber, Your Honour, with those at this point. I think it would be important if the issue of counsel could be resolved. That could lead us into discussions that could result in this case even not having a trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, that's something that's not for the Chamber up -- at least not at this moment to consider whether for other reasons there would be no need for trial. But since Rule 11 bis is in place, I just wanted to raise the issue and just wanted to see whether the parties had given it any thought. Mr. Cesic, a final issue I'd like to briefly discuss, and please tell me if you want to do this in private session or not, is whether you have any concerns about your health at this very moment that the Chamber and that the pre-trial judge should be informed about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at this moment. I have no health problems. Everything is in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cesic. As far as I can see, we have gone through all the items of the agenda apart from one, and that is that a 65 ter conference should be scheduled on short notice. And of course, I am aware that a potential -- possible change of counsel could make a 65 ter conference more complex and could create difficulties. But nevertheless, I would ask the parties, and I'd like to inform you, Mr. Cesic, that a 65 ter meeting, 65 ter meeting, would be scheduled for the second half of January. Is there anything else any of the parties or you, Mr. Cesic, would like to submit at this very moment? Let me first ask you. Anything else to be discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at this moment. Not until I submit a second request to change Defence counsel, then that would be something to discuss. But until then, I have nothing else to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you want to file a renewed request for change of Defence counsel. We'll wait and see what it contains. But a new request, I think, should be addressed to the Registry. If you would like to object against the decision taken, or at least the decision contained in the most recent letter of the Registry, of course another procedure would apply. You would have to request a review of that decision. Mr. Nedic, any -- thank you, Mr. Cesic. Any issue to be discussed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one: Despite the fact that this matter should be ruled upon by the Registry, I think that Mr. Cesic should be allowed to change Defence counsel. I must say that there have been no omissions made in preparation of his Defence case by his Defence counsel; however, there is no relationship of trust that should exist between an attorney and his client. Therefore, based on that, and based on the principle of ensuring the fairness of trial, I think that Mr. Cesic should be allowed to change his Defence counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's quite clear to me you reject whatever blame in your direction as far as your function as counsel is concerned. But at the same time, you say that the right to be assisted by counsel, preferably by counsel of choice, should be fully respected. And therefore, for these reasons, you think it proper to follow any request in this respect. Thank you. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have nothing to add. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes the Status Conference. It might have been the first Status Conference on a generator rather than under full power supply, but I think -- I would like to thank the parties for being as concise under these specific circumstances as was necessary. We'll adjourn, and a 65 ter meeting will be scheduled by the senior legal officer in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 9.38 a.m.
